illustrations.name: turret-base
illustrations.prompt: Edit target: the attached amber and graphite science-fiction energy turret sprite from a Korean 2.5D RPG. Draw only its STATIC FLOOR PEDESTAL for an articulated in-game sprite. Remove the whole moving upper weapon housing and its lens. A squat broad charcoal octagonal base and a short central pedestal with the exposed circular horizontal swivel seat on top, readable ellipse centered precisely over the base. Keep the distinctive beveled dark steel, copper fasteners and a few muted ochre armor panels from the reference. Low, stable posture, natural floor contact, vertical centerline upright. Orthographic 3/4 video game side view with camera about 32 degrees ABOVE the floor (the top of the turntable is visible). Aligned screen horizontal, no Dutch tilt, ellipse of the seat horizontally level. The pedestal including the socket is only about half as tall as it is wide, no tall pole. Painterly crisp game icon rendering matching the supplied reference, soft warm upper-left light, small contact darkening on the bottom rim. Exactly one isolated pedestal centered on transparent background, neatly framed with minimal padding and full edges, no ground tile, surrounding shadows, floating parts, words or captions. This will sit on an apartment floor.

illustrations.name: turret-heads
illustrations.prompt:
Edit target: the supplied amber and graphite turret sprite, a fictional AUTOMATED ENERGY PROJECTOR in a 2.5D Korean RPG. Make ONE transparent, professional GAME SPRITE TURNTABLE SHEET, precisely 3 columns x 2 rows, landscape 3:2. It contains exactly SIX separate cutouts of the SAME swiveling upper amber HEAD ONLY in six yaw directions. Omit the static floor base, lower pedestal and vertical column entirely from every cell; the head is the amber housing that will sit over a separate pedestal. All 6 are the exact same small rigid prop: slightly elongated amber armor shell, dark graphite trim, rear black radiator grille, BRIGHT amber rectangular aperture at its one projecting front end. Keep the identity, bevel design, scale, width and metallic style of the reference. Projector head has a more pronounced short nose forward of its centered black underside pivot, easy to tell the front from the rear. The head aims LEVEL and parallel to the virtual floor in every view. Fixed orthographic camera at 32 degrees above the floor, top panel visible in every view, carefully change yaw as on a real 3D turntable. Each column and row has equal-sized transparent cells, each cutout fitted comfortably and SEPARATED from its neighbors with wide clear gutters, centered in its tile. Absolutely no labels, arrows, guides, numbers, grid lines, shadows on an imaginary floor, background or base.
Top left cell: 3 O'CLOCK right side profile; muzzle at the far RIGHT screen edge, top panel and side visible. Top middle cell: 1:30 upper-right, AWAY from viewer. Nose on upper right, dark rear vent closest at lower left; only a sliver of amber at the forward end. Top right cell: 12 O'CLOCK straight away, rear grille faces the viewer at bottom center; nose extends behind toward the TOP of the tile, no glowing front visible.
Bottom left cell: 4:30 lower-right, TOWARD viewer. Nose and luminous aperture visible at lower right, dark rear upper left. Bottom middle cell: 6 O'CLOCK straight toward viewer, amber aperture faces us at the BOTTOM center; symmetrical top armor recedes away. Bottom right cell: 9 O'CLOCK left side profile; muzzle at far LEFT edge, closest flank broad and readable.
Same elevated camera and gentle upper-left light in all six tiles, each image is only the detachable upper housing, bottom edge complete, transparent margins. High-quality game art sharp at 96px.

illustrations.name: turret-inbetweens
illustrations.prompt:
Edit target and strict model reference: the attached 3x2 yaw sprite sheet of a single amber, boxy, swivelling science-fiction game turret HEAD. Draw its FOUR MISSING IN-BETWEEN TURN ANIMATION FRAMES as a 2x2 square sprite sheet on a fully transparent background. Match the SAME amber plates, dark graphite edges, rear black grille, front amber emitter and fixed elevated orthographic camera on the reference. Only the floating upper housing with its little underside socket, no floor pedestal or ground. These must be genuinely different intermediate orientations, precisely between the key views. Never turn the camera or the horizon. Distinct designed nose ending in an illuminated aperture, short blunt dark radiator at the rear.
TOP LEFT, near sideways facing RIGHT and a little AWAY: yaw 22.5 degrees from due right toward straight back. A broad side profile with a hint of the BACK END on the LEFT, projected long axis almost horizontal, nose only ~10 degrees above screen right. 
TOP RIGHT, nearly REAR view: yaw 22.5 degrees from straight BACK toward the right (NNE). Centered dark rear radiator very prominently facing the viewer in the foreground at the lower left, nose going into the distance toward the top right OF THE SAME CELL, very narrow right-going silhouette. We see only a thin sliver of the side. No front light facing the viewer. The longitudinal centerline seen on the top panels MUST angle only slightly right of straight up (~55 degrees above screen horizontal), much steeper screen angle than the supplied rear 3/4 view. 
BOTTOM LEFT, near sideways facing RIGHT and a little TOWARD camera: yaw 22.5 degrees from due right toward straight front (ESE), broad almost horizontal side, slight amber aperture on the RIGHT and slightly LOWER than the back. Projected long axis ~10 degrees below screen horizontal.
BOTTOM RIGHT, nearly FRONTAL: yaw 22.5 degrees from straight FRONT toward the right (SSE). Big amber front aperture nearly square-on to the camera, projecting slightly to lower RIGHT, rear receding behind toward upper LEFT. Narrow head, only one slim flank, long top panel points almost straight at the camera (about 55 degrees below screen horizontal in projection).
Use exactly four equally sized cells, center each object with clear transparent gutters; no panel dividers, lettering, digits, shadows, mounting pillar, spark effects or floor. Identical armor, scale and light from upper left across all four images. Each cell is a clean transparent sprite ready to visually interpolate the attached reference's six poses.
